rows.abstract: "Productivity AND PERFORMANCE Incentives and GAINSHARING Act of [1990] 1998".  Seeks to strengthen further the cooperation between labor and capital by ensuring workers of a just SHARE in the fruits of their labor in relation to the profit yielded to the employer.  The GAINSHARING SYSTEM may be in the form of (1) productivity bonus; (2) performance bonus; (3) production bonus; (4) employee stock option plan.
rows.status: Substituted by HB11809

rows.abstract: To make more meaningful the authority of the CHED, this bill designates the Chairman of the CHED as CHAIN of all SUCs governing boards, thereby allowing the Chair to assess priorities, programs and performance of all SUCs.

rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WOMEN since 1998-11-17

rows.author: B036
rows.title_full: AN ACT REGULATING THE WASTE DISPOSAL SYSTEM OF ALL GOVERNMENT AND PRIVATE HOSPITALS, MEDICAL CENTERS AND CLINICS, PRESCRIBING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATIONS THEREOF AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Requires all hospitals, medical centers and clinics to provide for its own waste disposal system to prevent environmental damage and unnecessary loss of valuable resources through RECOVERY, RECYCLING and RE-USE of waste and waste products.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 1998-11-17

rows.abstract: Requires every private sector employer to ensure that THREE PERCENT (3%) of his workforce, inclusive of managerial and supervisory personal, is composed of DISABLED PERSONS. Provides INCENTIVES to such employers. Penalizes violation of this Act.

rows.abstract: Rationale: Nonrecyclable materials DO NOT allow conversion into or extraction of reusable materials. This greatly exacerbates the country's waste management problem.
